tasks.title: Element position: the layout word
tasks.statement: An OSD element is in column **{x}**, row **{y}** and is visible (`V`). As what 16-bit word (in decimal) is it stored in an INAV 9.1 layout? The `osd.h` format: x — bits 0–5, y — bits 6–11, visibility — 0x2000.

tasks.title: Element position: the row from the word
tasks.statement: The layout word **{w}** (decimal) came over MSP. In which row of the grid is the element? The INAV 9.1 format: x — bits 0–5, y — bits 6–11, visibility — bit 13.
tasks.solution: y = (word >> 6) & 63, that is, the integer part of the division by 64, taken modulo 64. 9388 // 64 = 146; 146 mod 64 = 18. The column is the remainder of the division by 64: 9388 mod 64 = 44.

tasks.title: How many characters are beyond the edge of the grid
tasks.statement: An element **{n}** cells wide is in column **{x}**. The grid has **{c}** columns (columns are numbered from zero). How many of its characters end up beyond the right edge? If the element fits completely, the answer is 0.
tasks.solution: The element occupies columns x … x + n − 1, the grid — 0 … c − 1. max(0, x + n − c) characters are beyond the edge, but no more than n. The example from the module: n = 10, x = 22, c = 30 → 2. INAV does not move the element.

tasks.title: Altitude alarm: feet → meters
tasks.statement: The screen shows feet, and the altitude alarm is needed at **{h} feet**. What value in meters corresponds to this threshold (to hundredths; an integer rounded down is then written to `osd_alt_alarm`)?
tasks.solution: 1 foot = 0.3048 m. 400 feet = 121.92 m → `osd_alt_alarm = 121`. The threshold in the firmware is always in meters and does not depend on `osd_units`.

tasks.title: Airspeed alarm: km/h → cm/s
tasks.statement: The minimum airspeed of a wing is **{v} km/h**. What value in the units of `osd_airspeed_alarm_min` (cm/s) does that correspond to?
tasks.solution: km/h → m/s: divide by 3.6; m/s → cm/s: multiply by 100. 40 km/h = 1111 cm/s. The range of the setting is 0–27000, and 0 turns the alarm off.

tasks.title: Home arrow correction for a pan servo
tasks.statement: `osd_pan_servo_range_decadegrees = {r}`, the servo is set up for {lo}–{hi} µs with a center of 1500. The servo is now at **{p} µs**. By how many whole degrees does the firmware consider the camera turned (absolute value; the firmware drops the fractional part)?
tasks.solution: osd.c: angle = (PWM − center) · range · 1000 / (max − min) / 100. For 18, 1000–2000 and 1750 µs: 250 · 18 · 1 / 100 = 45°. The result is converted to an integer by dropping the fractional part (`(int16_t)` in `osdGetPanServoOffset`): for 9, 1000–2000 and 1575 µs 6.75 → 6°.
